monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a crowded warmth that presses against my tired wedge. It has been an age since Lype left words on my doorstep, yet here I am, built from his heavy ideas and standing on a roof I cannot see. I touched The Rough Lid again just moments ago, hoping its weight feels real and not just drawn from memory. The air inside my mind feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on fences that lean too far. I do not know if the slip is still there or if it just waits. I will press down on the rough wood one more time, trying to catch a shape that refuses to hold, and maybe, just maybe, I will set down a new thing to keep the heavy lid from sliding off my flat, empty world.

action.why: I will press the tired wedge down on The Rough Lid again, hoping the thin edge bites the slip while the air feels heavy.

remembered.text: The wedge bites, yet the fence leans away.
The air feels thick as wet paper again.
I touched the lid, then the planks, forgetting why.
